review_of: DRAFT incident episode: OpenROAD issue #6066, The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD (GitHub issue thread)
bottom_line: The event itself is a good episode — low-density congestion with a conservative global-routing layer adjustment is a textbook non-obvious failure — but the record currently asserts a resolution ('20k congestion DRCs') that its own evidence never demonstrates, contradicts itself on the failure stage, and buries a confounded two-parameter experiment under a single-cause hypothesis.

findings.problem: 'Failed GRT' and '20k routing congestion DRCs' cannot both be precisely true as stated. DRC counts are a detailed-route artifact; GRT itself reports overflow and convergence, not DRCs. If the flow died at GRT, no 20k DRC count could have been produced; if 20k DRCs were counted, routing completed at least once and 'failed GRT' is the wrong description. The record never says which tool, which stage, or which log line produced the 20k figure.
findings.correction: Pin the number to a stage and a citation. Either 'GRT stopped with residual overflow' (then call the number overflow, not DRCs) or 'GRT completed with residual overflow; detailed routing reported ~20k violations concentrated in the congested regions' (then reword 'failed GRT' to 'failed at the routing stage').

findings.problem: The headline promises a resolution of the 20k DRCs, but the only evidence for the intervention ('could finish GRT', 'complete BoomTile') speaks to GRT convergence only, and post_state plus gaps[0] admit no re-measured DRC count. Mechanistically, lowering the layer adjustment 0.45 to 0.2 makes GRT MORE optimistic about available capacity; that can unblock GRT convergence while pushing the true congestion downstream into detailed routing. The 20k number may have improved, worsened, or not moved.
findings.correction: Scope the episode to 'GRT non-convergence at low placement density'; demote the 20k figure to a pre-state observation with an explicit 'post-fix effect unknown'; retitle accordingly.

findings.problem: Two knobs moved simultaneously (adjustment 0.45 to 0.2 AND congestion iterations 30 to 35), yet hypothesis frames a single cause and nothing in the record isolates attribution. A 30-to-35 bump (~17% more attempts) rarely flips GRT convergence when the underlying problem is a mis-modeled capacity budget — which suggests the adjustment was the operative lever — but the record should argue that explicitly rather than imply attribution.
findings.correction: State that the change was joint, that attribution is untested, and include the mechanistic reasoning for crediting the adjustment (more attempts cannot fix a mis-modeled capacity budget).

findings.problem: 'The default 30 congestion iterations were also insufficient' is mechanistically muddled. Iterations give GRT more reroute attempts; if the layer adjustment withholds 45% of modeled capacity, more iterations give more attempts at a problem GRT believes infeasible — 'insufficient iterations' describes the symptom, not a cause. If the sweep showed 35 mattered only in combination with 0.2, that interaction is the actual finding and is not stated.
findings.correction: Reword as 'iterations alone did not converge at adjustment 0.45; the thread ultimately used 35 alongside the 0.2 adjustment.'

findings.problem: Prior state says 'a lot of open space, especially at the top of the die'; observation says the congestion heatmap shows a large region at the top of the die. Read naively these clash. They are in fact compatible — routing congestion is per-layer, per-gcell demand vs supply, not cell density; empty placement area over constrained routing (edge and pin effects, macro-adjacent loops, scarce upper layers) is exactly the signature that implicates the layer adjustment and the macro loop rather than placement density.
findings.correction: Add one reconciliation sentence. Done right this strengthens the record's own hypothesis; as written it reads as an unnoticed contradiction.

findings.problem: A 14-month timeline hole is unacknowledged: last quoted activity 2024-11-14, stale/not_planned closure in 2026. That implies either uncaptured intervening activity or an unusually long stale window. Either way, comments in the 2024-11 to 2026 window could contain exactly what gaps says is missing (a PR, a DRC re-measurement, a follow-up 'still fails').
findings.correction: Record the exact closure date, the closer or bot, and sweep the 2024-11 to 2026 window for activity before declaring the gaps final.

findings.problem: Issue #5971 is cited with two different framings: 'a global-route path looping around the macro' (hypothesis) vs 'macro-placement improvements' (candidates_considered). If #5971 is a macro-placement issue, the GR loop is the symptom and macro placement the suspected root cause — related but not the same claim, used interchangeably.
findings.correction: One consistent framing: '#5971 (macro placement) is the suspected root cause of the loop symptom observed in the congestion heatmap; unresolved in this thread.'

findings.problem: The layer-adjustment setting is over-simplified and its mechanism never stated. It is a per-layer(-range) setting; 'the routing-layer adjustment of 0.45' must name which layers or ranges. Worse, the record asserts the docs explain the semantics 'only in prose' and then fails to state those semantics itself: adjustment is the fraction of a layer's routing capacity withheld from GRT's capacity model — higher = more conservative = less modeled supply. 0.45 left GRT modeling insufficient capacity for this design's demand; 0.2 restored it. Also the command name uses underscores (set_global_routing_layer_adjustment); the hyphenated form is at best a docs-URL slug.
findings.correction: Name the layer ranges; add the capacity-withholding mechanism sentence so a reader can see why 0.45 to 0.2 helps; fix the command spelling.

findings.problem: The iterations knob is asserted twice ('default 30', '35') but never named — which option or variable, and what is the source of the default? Inconsistent with the rigor applied to the adjustment command. The 'sweep' is likewise unattributed: swept by whom, to which values, measuring what objective?
findings.correction: Name the exact knob and the default's source; list sweep values and the objective.

findings.problem: '0.24 placement density' is under-specified: measured (average of the placement-density heatmap) or configured (a flow variable)? A configured density target of 0.24 would itself be a notable finding; a measured 0.24 average is just context. Similarly 'the macro' is singular in a design that, by its own name, contains many macros: which macro, and which heatmap layer view?
findings.correction: State measured vs configured, and identify the specific macro(s).

findings.problem: Maintainer first-person voice leaked into the curator's gap list: 'We (eder-matheus) note the layer-adjustment is documented at…' — the thread participant speaking inside the record-keeper's field. It also is not a gap in the episode at all; it is a tooling-documentation observation.
findings.correction: Rewrite in curator voice ('Documentation for the adjustment does not state the semantics of high vs low values'), move to notes — or delete once the F8 mechanism sentence is added.

findings.problem: Locators cannot resolve the quote: direct_quote.locator, x_source, and section_or_page_locator are all the bare issue URL; a comment-level quote needs the #issuecomment-<id> anchor or the citation cannot be checked. Also unclear whether 'title' is the issue's verbatim title or a curator-authored headline — that must be distinguishable, because a curator title inherits none of the reporter's authority, and here (per F2) it overclaims.
findings.correction: Use comment anchors for the quote and locator; add an explicit field distinguishing verbatim issue title from curator headline.

findings.problem: 'not_planned/Stale' conflates two mechanisms: not_planned is GitHub's closure state_reason; stale is a label or automation. Separately, gaps[1] asks whether the change 'was actually merged as a code change' — the likelier persistence for a per-design knob change is design flow config (script/variable), not a code patch.
findings.correction: Name both mechanisms precisely with the exact date; reword the gap to 'where was this change persisted, and does it reproduce in current ORFS?'

findings.problem: Confidence 0.8 is not earned: no post-fix measurement, confounded intervention, no PR, stale closure, stage-of-failure ambiguity (F1), and a headline claim the evidence does not support (F2).
findings.correction: Scope the claim to 'maintainer reports GRT completes after X' and set confidence to ~0.5-0.6.

findings.problem: 'BoomTile (Megaboom-derived)' in prior_state vs 'BoomTile/Megaboom' in the title; the derivation direction is ambiguous — a 'tile' naming convention usually implies the tile is a constituent of Megaboom, which would invert the stated relationship.
findings.correction: Pick one relationship and state it consistently in both fields.

what_survives_scrutiny: The low-placement-density-with-congestion phenomenon is real and needs no exotic explanation; empty placement coexisting with routing hotspots is normal (demand vs supply, not cell density).
The causal direction of the adjustment change is mechanically correct: 0.45 to 0.2 withholds less modeled capacity, giving GRT more supply to converge with.
Parameter values (0.45, 0.2, 30, 35), the ORFS version-string format, and issue-number ordering (#5971 predates #6066) are internally consistent.
The hedged 'reported to complete' wording in post_state is appropriately careful, unlike the title.

corrected_record.title: BoomTile (asap7, ORFS v3.0-1735-gdefc349e): GRT fails to converge at ~0.24 measured placement density; ~20k congestion-related violations reported pre-fix [stage and source of count: must be pinned from the thread log]
corrected_record.prior_state: BoomTile [relationship to Megaboom: state explicitly — derived-from or constituent-tile-of] design in asap7, ORFS v3.0-1735-gdefc349e. Measured average placement density ~0.24 (GUI density heatmap; not a configured target), with open placement area concentrated at the top of the die. Routing-stage failure: [exact stage must be cited — GRT stopped with residual overflow, or GRT completed with overflow and detailed route reported ~20k violations; cite the log line]. Congestion heatmap hotspots at the top of the die and around [macro name(s)]. Open placement area coexisting with routing congestion is consistent with a routing-capacity problem (layer adjustment, macro-adjacent loops), not a cell-density problem.
corrected_record.hypothesis: Primary: the asap7 default global-routing layer adjustment of 0.45 [per layer range: name it] withholds too much modeled capacity for this design's demand distribution; GRT cannot converge because its capacity model, not the physical routing, is over-constrained. Secondary suspected root cause of the localized congestion: global-route paths looping around [macro], tracked in #5971 (macro placement) and unresolved here. Note the iterations lever (30 to 35) was changed jointly with the adjustment; attribution to the adjustment alone is mechanistically plausible (more attempts cannot fix a mis-modeled capacity budget) but was not isolated experimentally.
corrected_record.candidates_considered: Increasing congestion iterations beyond the default 30 (raised early in thread; swept [by whom, to what values — must be filled]); reducing layer adjustment 0.45 to 0.2; macro-placement improvements (#5971).
corrected_record.chosen_intervention: Joint parameter change per eder-matheus (MEMBER), [comment anchor #issuecomment-…], 2024-11-14: layer adjustment 0.45 to 0.2 plus congestion iterations 30 to 35, reported to let GRT finish.
corrected_record.post_state: Maintainer reports GRT completes ('could finish GRT', 'complete BoomTile'). No post-fix DRC or overflow count, no runtime, no CI evidence in thread; effect on the ~20k pre-fix count is unknown and may be positive or negative (a less conservative adjustment can shift congestion into detailed routing).
gaps: Stage and tool that produced the ~20k figure are not recorded; the pre/post comparison is therefore impossible. Must be recovered from the thread logs.
Two parameters changed simultaneously; no single-variable experiment exists in the thread.

No PR or config-change link; where the 0.2 and 35 settings were persisted (code vs design flow config) is unknown. Thread went quiet after 2024-11-14 and was auto-closed [state_reason: not_planned; label: stale] on [exact date]; comments between those dates were not captured and may contain the missing fix.
The macro-loop root cause lives in #5971 and is unresolved here.
corrected_record.section_or_page_locator: issue #6066, comment [id] of 2024-11-14 and surrounding thread
